rationale: fp-convert is a tiny, hot floating-point conversion kernel (SingleSource/Misc) with no meaningful static profile, few calls, and little global state, so the cheapest high-value passes are favored: SUB gets the highest weights because arithmetic substitution is nearly free at runtime/size and is very effective on numeric code, with only modest FP-semantic risk; FLA is next since dispatch-loop flattening strongly resumes static analysis of a small control-flow graph at tolerable overhead; SPLIT and IBR are kept at moderate weights as cheap diversity boosters that complement FLA/SUB; BCF is down-weighted heavily because its bogus-block cloning multiplies size and runtime in a tight loop that dominates this benchmark's execution; ICALL and IGV are retained at low weights only because the program's near-absence of indirect-callable targets and global variables means they would add call/indirection overhead and correctness exposure with minimal security return, letting the per-function selector effectively skip them.
